Article Title: 17.4 lakh blood components discarded in 2025 despite record collection
Article Text:
India discarded over 17.4 lakh blood components in 2025

NEW DELHI: India discarded over 17.4 lakh blood components in 2025, even as blood collection reached a record 1.58 crore units, according to state-wise data tabled in the Rajya Sabha, highlighting continued challenges in blood inventory management despite a steady rise in donations.Available official data indicate that China and India are among the world's largest blood collection programmes. In 2025, India collected 15.71 million units of blood, while China collected 25.5 million units, according to China's National Health Commission.The data, reported by blood centres through the government's e-Raktakosh portal, show that expiry was the leading reason for discarding blood components, followed by reactive units and other operational reasons. Reason-wise discard data has been captured on the portal since 2024, while such details were not available for 2023.Replying to a question in Parliament, the Union health ministry, however, said it had not received any report of regional blood shortages. It added that ensuring an adequate supply of safe blood and minimising wastage is primarily the responsibility of state governments and Union Territories, while the Centre advocates a hub-and-spoke model under which blood is collected and processed at high-volume centres before being distributed to smaller blood banks and storage centres.According to the data, Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest blood collection in 2025 with 21.6 lakh units, followed by Maharashtra (18.73 lakh), Gujarat (11.82 lakh), Rajasthan (10.79 lakh) and Tamil Nadu (9.74 lakh). Overall blood collection increased from 1.42 crore units in 2023 to 1.58 crore units in 2025.The annexure also showed a corresponding increase in blood component utilisation, with Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan reporting the highest utilisation during 2025.At the same time, Uttar Pradesh reported the highest discard of blood components at 2.40 lakh, followed by Maharashtra (1.87 lakh), Kerala (1.44 lakh), Rajasthan (1.21 lakh) and Tamil Nadu (1.09 lakh). The ministry did not provide an analysis of the wide variation in discard across states.Dr Hema Goyal, Consultant (Blood centre & Lab services), Aakash healthcare said blood wastage is inevitable to some extent, particularly because platelets have a shelf life of only five days. But discarding 17.4 lakh blood components in a year points to a mismatch between collection and actual demand. The solution is not fewer donations but smarter inventory management through real-time stock sharing and better coordination between blood banks.
Article Summary: India discarded over 17.4 lakh blood components in 2025. Blood collection reached a record 1.58 crore units, state-wise data tabled in rajya sabha. Expiry was the leading reason for discarding blood components, followed by reactive units.

Article Title: FSSAI pulls up two popular food products over safety, compliance lapses

NEW DELHI: In a fresh crackdown on food safety violations, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has acted against two food products, penalising the manufacturer of a fortified sunflower oil after it was found to be substandard and stopping the sale of a Monk Fruit Sweetener over alleged licensing and labelling violations.The regulator imposed a penalty on AWL Agri Business Ltd, Mangaluru, after a laboratory analysis of a retail sample of Fortune "Fryola" Refined Sunflower Seed Oil found that its vitamin D content was below the prescribed standard, making the fortified edible oil substandard under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.FSSAI said the company was given an opportunity to present its case, but the adjudicating authority concluded that it had manufactured and marketed a substandard fortified edible oil before imposing a monetary penalty.In a separate action, the regulator prohibited the sale of PIE Foods' Monk Fruit Sweetener, a natural zero-calorie sugar substitute, after inspections found cartons of the product stored at the company's premises without the required manufacturing licence.FSSAI also alleged that the product carried claims such as "100% Monk Fruit Extract" and "Natural Ingredients", while its online listing did not carry the mandatory endorsement required under food safety regulations.It further said the company failed to produce records showing that the monk fruit extract used in the product had been procured in accordance with the Food Safety and Standards Act.The prohibition order will remain in force until the product complies with the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act and related regulations.The regulator said the actions are part of its ongoing drive to tighten enforcement against food business operators and ensure that products sold to consumers meet prescribed safety and quality standards.
Article Summary: The food safety and standards authority of india (fssai) has acted against two food products. The regulator penalised the manufacturer of a fortified sunflower oil after it was found to be substandard. It also stopped the sale of a monk fruit sweetener over alleged licensing and labelling violations.

Article Title: 'Power Banks' for satellites? Bengaluru Company builds tech to keep ageing spacecraft alive
Article Text:

BENGALURU: What if satellites could simply plug into a power bank instead of drifting away when they run out of fuel? That’s the idea driving a Bengaluru startup building “jetpack” satellites designed to latch onto ageing spacecraft, take over their propulsion duties and keep billion-dollar assets working years longer.After recently validating a key part of its technology at an Isro facility used for India’s SpaDeX docking mission, Aule Space is now preparing for what could become one of the world’s most ambitious private satellite docking demonstrations.For satellite operators, running out of fuel doesn’t necessarily mean spacecraft have reached the end of life. In many cases, expensive communication satellites remain fully functional, but can no longer maintain their assigned orbital positions because they have exhausted the propellant needed for station-keeping. Once that happens, operators are forced to retire assets worth hundreds of millions of dollars.Aule has found another way. “We’re trying to build satellites which can go and dock to existing satellites in space which don’t have any installed ports... and extend their life so that they can keep generating revenue,” CEO Jay Panchal, told TOI. “It’s like a power bank,” he added.Instead of attempting the far more complicated task of refuelling satellites in orbit, Aule’s approach is to send a smaller “jetpack” spacecraft that docks with an existing communications satellite and assumes responsibility for station-keeping using its own propulsion system.The company plans to target geostationary communication satellites, many of which cost more than $300 million to build and generate significant annual revenues.The challenge lies in docking with satellites that were never designed to be serviced. Rather than relying on dedicated docking ports, Aule will attach its spacecraft to the liquid apogee motor (LAM) nozzle, a standard external feature found on most geostationary satellites.If successful, the technology could help operators extract years of additional service from satellites that would otherwise become orbital relics. Panchal said each docked “jetpack” could extend a satellite’s operational life by up to 5 years.*Key Test Done*The startup recently completed a major milestone by testing its camera-based guidance, navigation and control system at the Rendezvous Simulation Laboratory (RSL) at Isro’s ISITE — the same lab where critical elements of the SpaDeX were validated.“We were the first non-govt entity to access RSL. This is the best kind of on-ground testing we can do for these capabilities,” Panchal said.One of Aule’s differentiators is its reliance on computer vision instead of multiple specialised sensors. Current docking systems typically use LiDAR, infrared cameras and other sensors. Aule says its spacecraft will perform the critical final approach using a single optical camera powered by onboard AI.The visual navigation models are trained using data generated in its own facilities and validated at Isro’s testbed before being deployed in orbit.The company is targeting an in-orbit demonstration next year, when it plans to launch two satellites that will autonomously dock in low-Earth orbit. Panchal claims it could be the world’s first private mission to perform non-cooperative docking in LEO using camera-only navigation. The mission will validate technologies that Aule ultimately intends to deploy around geostationary communication satellites.
Article Summary: Bengaluru startup building ‘jetpack’ satellites designed to latch onto ageing spacecraft. Aule space preparing for what could become one of the world’s most ambitious private satellite docking demonstrations. Company plans to target geostationary communication satellites, many of which cost more than $300 million to build.

Article Text:
The panel, it said, shall devise suitable norms and guidelines 'keeping in view the cultural ethos and sensitivity of the country'

NEW DELHI: The information and broadcasting (I&B) ministry has told a parliamentary committee that it is mulling a comprehensive statutory framework to regulate the airing of programmes on OTT platforms, "which are offensive to moral standards of society", without infringing upon the rights and freedom of individuals.The department-related standing committee on the ministry of home affairs, in its recommendations in the 259th report tabled in Parliament on Friday, said the proposed comprehensive statutory framework for regulating OTT content must incorporate robust technology-enabled age verification mechanisms, effective parental controls and suitable penalties for non-compliance.While observing that the existing framework continued to rely largely on self-regulation by OTT platforms, the committee - in its recommendations on the action taken on its 254th report - reiterated that the government examine the feasibility of establishing an independent post-release review panel - comprising experts from fields like child development, education, law, social sciences and civil society - to review flagged OTT content and lay down appropriate corrective measures.The panel had, in its 254th report, said, "OTT platforms have emerged as a primary source of entertainment in India, with a reach that surpasses traditional cinema, including a substantial audience of minors." The committee pointed out that unlike films, which require mandatory pre-certification under the Cinematograph Act, OTT content operates under a self-classification system with post-release grievance redressal as per the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021.The panel said that although the aforesaid rules require age ratings, parental controls and a grievance mechanism, the lack of pre-release checks and weak age verification still leaves minors exposed to harmful content. Accordingly, it recommended that the government consider establishing a recognised panel of experts who will monitor new OTT releases.It suggested that the post-release review panel watch the flagged or trending content based on user complaints submitted through a standardised grievance mechanism.The panel, it said, shall devise suitable norms and guidelines "keeping in view the cultural ethos and sensitivity of the country". It recommended that the panel also work out suitable penalties for infringement of these norms/guidelines.
Article Summary: The department-related standing committee on the ministry of home affairs made its recommendations in the 259th report tabled in parliament on friday. The panel, it said, shall devise suitable norms and guidelines 'keeping in view the cultural ethos and sensitivity of the country'

Article Title: 'Stop buying petrol, diesel vehicles until govt clarifies stand': Arvind Kejriwal over E20 fuel concerns
Article Text:
"Stop buying petrol, diesel vehicles until govt clarifies stand": Arvind Kejriwal over E20 fuel concerns

Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Friday appealed to people to stop buying petrol and diesel vehicles until the government makes its stand clear on E20 fuel.Kejriwal alleged that the government had not conducted proper testing for E20 fuel and claimed that its implementation had led to a significant drop in the mileage of vehicles.He said the mileage of two-wheelers, motorcycles, scooters, cars, SUVs and other four-wheelers had dropped by around 25-30 per cent.Addressing a press conference in Goa, Kejriwal said, "Till such a time, the government makes its intention clear, I appeal to the people to stop buying petrol and diesel vehicles. The government did not conduct any testing for E20 fuel."Kejriwal said people in Goa were particularly affected by the decision, claiming that around 45 per cent of families in the state own a car and around 86 per cent of people own a two-wheeler.He said around 85-90 per cent of families in Goa could be affected by the decision due to the high ownership of vehicles in the state."The Modi government has aggressively implemented E20 across the country. People across the country are very unhappy about it. The mileage of two-wheelers, motorcycles, scooters, cars, SUVs, and four-wheelers has dropped significantly. There has been an almost 25-30 per cent drop in mileage...Peoplein Goa are disproportionately affected by this decision. Nationally, only around 7% of households own a car, but in Goa, almost 45 per cent of families own a car. Around 86 per cent of people in Goa own a two-wheeler. Obviously, there is some overlap, many households own both a four-wheeler and a two-wheeler. So, we can understand that around 85-90 per cent of families in Goa are affected by this decision," Kejriwal said.Kejriwal said countries that adopted E20 fuel took several years to fully implement the policy, citing Brazil as an example.He said Brazil introduced E5 in 1931 and E20 in 1985, taking around 50-55 years to move from E5 to E20. He added that Brazil had only recently moved towards E100, using pure ethanol with flex-fuel vehicles that can run without petrol.He added, "Around the world, countries that implemented E20 gave themselves 10, 15, or even 20 years before fully implementing the policy. Brazil is at the forefront. Brazil now uses E100, meaning pure ethanol is also used, with flex-fuel vehicles that can run without petrol. But Brazil took 50 years to move to E20. In 1931, Brazil introduced E5, and in 1985, it introduced E20. It took them 50-55 years to reach E20. And only now have they moved to E100. " (ANI)
Article Summary: "stop buying petrol, diesel vehicles until govt clarifies stand": arvind kejriwal over e20 fuel concerns. Kejriwal alleged that the government had not conducted proper testing for e20. He said the mileage of two-wheelers, motorcycles, scooters, cars, suvs and other four- wheelers had dropped by around 25-30 per cent.

Article Title: Astrobase unveils 800kN rocket engine, eyes reusability
Article Text:
Astrobase unveils India's first privately-built 800kN full-flow staged combustion rocket engine 'Everest', aiming for reusable launch systems and domestic launch infrastructure.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Space start-up Astrobase Space Technologies Friday unveiled what it described as India’s first privately built “800kN Full-Flow Staged Combustion (FFSC) liquid oxygen-methane rocket engine, named ‘Everest’”, as it seeks to develop reusable launch systems and expand domestic launch infrastructure.The Bengaluru-based company said the engine is designed for medium-lift launch vehicles and forms part of its long-term plan to build an integrated launch ecosystem covering propulsion, manufacturing, testing and launch operations. The next major milestone for the programme will be a full-engine hot-fire test, followed by vehicle integration and orbital launch development.According to the company: “Everest uses the full-flow staged combustion cycle, one of the most complex rocket engine architectures, and is powered by liquid oxygen and methane. The engine has been designed for reusability and offers 800 kN of thrust, a specific impulse of around 340 seconds and a throttle range of 50% to 110%.”The company said it plans to manufacture up to 50 engines annually once its facilities are fully operational, with the capability to hot-fire about one engine every week. It aims to test around 20 engines before attempting its first orbital mission.Its first phase of expansion is intended to support about 100 tonnes of annual launch capacity, with a longer-term goal of exceeding 1,000 tonnes through a higher launch cadence.It also said it was “working towards a launch-on-demand capability that could enable a dedicated mission within 15 days of an urgent national requirement. These targets are yet to be demonstrated”.Astrobase co-founder Neeraj Khandelwal said the engine was intended to establish an industrial capability rather than serve only as a technology demonstrator, adding that India would require indigenous high-thrust propulsion systems as satellite launches increase globally.IN-SPACe director (technical) Rajeev Jyoti said Astrobase was among the recipients of IN-SPACe’s Technology Adoption Fund, which is supporting development of the 800 kN engine. He said the programme, as it progresses through development and testing, could contribute to India’s launch capability and create new opportunities in the global space economy.Founded in 2024, Astrobase is developing propulsion systems, test infrastructure and reusable launch technologies from its Bengaluru base.
Article Summary: Astrobase unveils india's first privately-built 800kn full-flow staged combustion rocket engine 'everest' the engine is designed for medium-lift launch vehicles and forms part of its long-term plan to build an integrated launch ecosystem covering propulsion, manufacturing, testing and launch operations.

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Friday said Congress will soon take up the issue of the Centre's E20 ethanol-blended fuel programme.In a social media post on X, Rahul shared a video and accused the government of "stealing directly out of people's pockets"."This E20 issue is a very serious matter. Usually, we say, 'Daal mein kuch kaala hai.' But here, the whole daal is black," the Congress leader said."Brothers and sisters, this is a matter of priorities. In any campaign, we have to decide the order in which issues are taken up. The problem right now is that there is so much corruption that there is a long list of issues we have to prioritise. But don't worry. We will take up the E20 issue in a big way because it is damaging people's cars and scooters and their lives and is, quite literally, stealing money directly out of their pockets," he added.The remarks came days after Congress alleged that the Centre's push for E20 petrol had increased fuel costs for consumers while primarily benefiting ethanol producers, claiming motorists were paying more despite assurances of cheaper fuel.Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said that since March 2025, regular fuel stations across the country had been supplying "practically only E20 petrol".Referring to earlier statements by Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari, he said the government had claimed ethanol blending would bring the price of diesel down to Rs 50 per litre and provide a petrol alternative at Rs 55 per litre, but no such reduction had materialised."On the contrary, according to an independent analysis, between April 2023 and March 2026, consumers collectively spent an additional approximately Rs 88,234 crore to compensate for the lower mileage from ethanol-blended fuel," he wrote in a post on X.He further claimed that the Centre could have reduced the retail price of E20 petrol to offset the lower fuel efficiency and noted that NITI Aayog's Ethanol Roadmap had recommended financial and tax incentives for E10 and E20 fuels to compensate consumers."E20 has stripped the average middle-class Indian of options, imposed higher fuel costs on them, and placed an extra burden on the very vehicle they saved for years to buy. If any segment has benefited the most from E20, it is the ethanol producers," Ramesh said.However, the Centre has maintained that ethanol blending helps reduce India's dependence on imported crude oil and supports farmers by creating demand.

Scientists have used artificial intelligence to design viruses that exist nowhere in nature, and 16 of them turned out to be fully functional killers of bacteria. The work, published Thursday in the journal Science by a team at Stanford University and the Arc Institute in California, is the first time an AI model has written the complete instruction manual for a living thing rather than just one piece of it. The viruses in question only attack bacteria and cannot infect people, animals or plants.That last bit is the reassuring part, and everyone involved knows how thin it sounds. The same study that promises a new weapon against superbugs also proves that software trained on DNA can now dream up a working virus from a blank page. Two researchers at Johns Hopkins, Thomas Inglesby and Moritz Hanke, put it plainly in a commentary published alongside it: the ability to write viral genomes with AI now exists, and the rules to control it do not.The models, called Evo 1 and Evo 2, work a lot like ChatGPT. ChatGPT guesses which word comes next. Evo guesses which chemical letter comes next in a strand of DNA, which uses an alphabet of just four letters: A, C, G and T. Feed it enough genetic code and it starts picking up the grammar of life the way a chatbot picks up English.The team, led by Stanford's Brian Hie, trained it on millions of natural genomes, then focused it on one very well-studied virus called ΦX174 and its relatives.Evo spat out hundreds of thousands of possible designs. The researchers picked around 300, had the DNA physically made in a lab, and slipped it into bacteria—which obediently read the instructions and built the viruses themselves.Graduate student Samuel King spotted it in the early hours of the morning. Bacteria growing on a petri dish form a cloudy film, and when a virus is chewing through them, clear spots appear. The spots appeared. When he told the rest of the team, Hie recalls, "the room spontaneously burst into applause."The 16 that survived were not weak imitations. Some multiplied faster than the natural virus they were modelled on. And in the most useful result of the lot, a mix of the AI-designed viruses wiped out E. coli that had already learned to resist the natural version. A comparable mix of viruses collected from nature could not. Bacteria evolve to survive whatever we throw at them—this suggests we can now design new threats faster than they can adapt.They kept anything dangerous out of the training data. No viruses that infect humans, animals, plants or fungi went in, so the model has never seen what a human pathogen looks like. They used a harmless strain of E. coli and worked in a secure lab. Hanke called the caution commendable, while noting the team had no official rulebook to follow.A new US health policy issued last week bans making biological agents more dangerous, but it doesn't cover work done on a computer. And Evo 2 is open source, free for anyone to download, which has alarmed plenty of people.Others say the panic is early. Tom Ellis at Imperial College London called this the smallest, simplest genome anyone could have attempted. Size backs him up: this virus needs about 5,400 letters of code. The simplest living cell needs 500,000. Hie says going bigger would be "a lot of work, but not impossible"—which isn't exactly comforting.
Article Summary: Scientists have used artificial intelligence to design viruses that exist nowhere in nature. 16 of them turned out to be fully functional killers of bacteria. The work is the first time an ai model has written the complete instruction manual for a living thing. The viruses in question only attack bacteria and cannot infect people, animals or plants.

Article Title: US judge compares Meta to 'public nuisance,' orders $567m payout over child harm
Article Text:
US judge has ordered Meta to pay $567m in a New Mexico child safety case, ruling that Instagram and Facebook exposed children to harmful content and sexual exploitation

India is facing its own Meta child-safety concerns

Meta has been ordered to pay another $567 million by a US judge over allegations that its social media platforms exposed children to harmful content and failed to adequately protect young users.The ruling by Judge Bryan Biedscheid adds to mounting legal and regulatory pressure on Meta over the way Instagram and Facebook are designed and how they protect children from harmful content, sexual exploitation and potentially addictive use.The judge described Meta as a “public nuisance”, comparing the harm caused to children by its platforms to pollution produced by a factory. The money will be placed in a fund aimed at addressing the damage and preventing further harm.Meta, which owns Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp and Threads, rejected the ruling and said it would appeal.“We disagree with the ruling and will appeal,” a Meta spokesperson said, adding that the company works to keep people safe and remains confident in its record of protecting teenagers online.The latest order follows a $375 million civil penalty previously imposed in the same case, bringing the total financial liability to $942 million.The New Mexico case began with allegations that Meta's platforms exposed young users to sexually explicit material and enabled contact with sexual predators.The court had earlier found that Meta's recommendation systems directed young users towards harmful content and contacts. In the latest phase, the judge ruled that the resulting harms met the legal threshold of a public nuisance.The judge has also ordered a series of measures aimed at limiting risks to children. These include restrictions on interactions between adults and underage users, stronger safeguards against child sexual exploitation, limits on notifications and measures to reduce excessive use of Instagram and Facebook by minors.A significant portion of the $567 million fund — $420 million — will go towards treatment and behavioural-health programmes addressing harms that have already occurred. Other money will support prevention and training for teachers and health professionals.The ruling comes as Meta faces thousands of lawsuits in the US involving alleged harms to children and teenagers. The company has also faced legal challenges over whether the design of its platforms encourages addictive use among young people.The US ruling comes at a particularly relevant moment for Meta in India, where authorities have recently scrutinised the company over child safety on Instagram.In July, India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology ordered Instagram to disable advertisements and content promoting or facilitating access to child sexual abuse material, after reports that such material had appeared in paid advertisements on the platform. The ministry also sought an explanation from Meta.Meta subsequently acknowledged reports about Instagram advertisements in India that violated its policies against child exploitation. The company said its systems had already identified and removed some of the offending advertisements and accounts, while a subsequent investigation led to further removals and blocked URLs. Meta denied that it knowingly targeted such advertisements at users based on inappropriate interests.
Article Summary: Us judge has ordered meta to pay $567m in a new mexico child safety case, ruling that instagram and facebook exposed children to harmful content and sexual exploitation. The money will be placed in a fund aimed at addressing the damage and preventing further harm.

Article Title: Zohran Mamdani sends cease-and-desist notice to Amazon, Walmart and 40 other companies; says: Stop selling ...
Article Text:
Zohran Mamdani

Rising fatalities reason behind Zohran Mamdani’s notice to Amazon, Walmart and others

Elon Musk is not pleased with Zohran Mamdani's grocery stores idea

What is Zohran Mamdani's grocery store plan

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has issued a cease and desist notices to 42 online retailers including Amazon , Walmart, Target, Wayfair and Temu parent PDD Holdings, over the sale of allegedly illegal high-speed e-bikes and e-scooters. Mamdani said that the crackdown was important to protect public safety. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Mamdani stated, “Too many lives have been cut short by high-speed, illegal e-bikes and e-scooters. That’s why we are issuing cease-and-desist orders against 42 online retailers that have been selling these dangerous devices to New York City residents — including Target, Temu, Wayfair, Walmart, and Amazon. The safety of New Yorkers is not for sale.” The city said the targeted devices exceed legal limits for speed, weight, or other safety requirements. The action follows a recent crash involving an illegal e-bike that killed a 17-year-old.According to city data, since 2017 more than 45 people have died while riding illegal e-bikes, and over 14 fatalities have been linked to crashes involving illegal stand-up scooters.Mamdani emphasized that companies profiting from such sales are putting New Yorkers at risk. “Every family deserves to know that when their loved ones leave home, they will make it back safely,” he said.Recently, Tesla CEO Elon Musk criticised New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani over his plan to open city-backed grocery stores that promise to sell some everyday food items at prices below traditional retailers. Responding to a post on X (formerly Twitter) that questioned how the proposed stores would operate, Elon Musk dismissed the plan and accused Mamdani of misleading New Yorkers. “Mamdani is a thief and a liar, plain and simple,” Musk wrote in the post. The billionaire also argued that advances in AI and robotics, rather than government-backed programmes, would eventually make goods and services much cheaper or even free.Zohran Mamdani's administration has proposed opening five city-backed grocery stores, with one planned for each of New York City's five boroughs. The city has allocated $70 million in capital funding for the programme. The first store is expected to open in Hunts Point in the Bronx by the end of 2027, followed by locations in East Harlem, Brooklyn, Queens and Staten Island.Under the proposal, private grocery operators would handle day-to-day operations, including staffing, sourcing products and merchandising. The city would provide locations, cover major occupancy costs and set pricing and operating requirements. Mamdani's administration says shoppers could save about 30% on a core basket of groceries. It estimates that the programme could save an average New Yorker about $90 a month, or roughly $1,000 a year.

The action follows a recent crash involving an illegal e-bike that killed a 17-year-old. Since 2017 more than 45 people have died while ridingillegal e-bikes.

Article Title: As world’s oldest lightbulb turns 125 years old, conspiracy theorists have a 'cover up' theory
Article Text:

"cover-up"

"cover-up"

Why the Centennial Bulb has lasted so long

How the Phoebus Cartel fuelled the conspiracy theory

Why modern bulbs took a different path

"cover-up."

A light bulb has been glowing for the past 125 years. The milestone is once again drawing attention, not only for its longevity but also because conspiracy theorists claim it exposes a decades-longby major light bulb manufacturers. The Centennial Bulb in Livermore, California, is frequently cited as evidence that companies deliberately reduced the lifespan of light bulbs through planned obsolescence, although engineers and historians say its unusual design tells a different story.According to a Popular Science report, the renewed discussion comes as the Centennial Bulb marks 125 years since it was first switched on in 1901. While thetheory points to the light's unusually long life compared with modern incandescent bulbs, experts say its low power consumption, dim output and unique construction explain why it has continued operating for so long, rather than proving that manufacturers intentionally hid longer-lasting technology.The Centennial Bulb was manufactured by Ohio-based Shelby Electric Company in 1901 and has remained installed at Livermore Fire Station No. 6 in California. It was recognised by Guinness World Records and Ripley's Believe It or Not in 1972 as the oldest known working light bulb.Unlike modern incandescent bulbs, which were later standardised to operate at higher brightness, the Centennial Bulb now draws only about four watts of power despite originally being designed as a 60-watt bulb.Because it operates at a much lower temperature, its tungsten filament deteriorates far more slowly than that of a conventional incandescent lamp.Early incandescent bulbs were handmade, and manufacturers often prioritised durability over brightness. Their filaments were enclosed inside sealed glass bulbs, where an electric current heated the metal until it emitted visible light. However, increasing brightness also increased filament temperature, accelerating wear and shortening the bulb's lifespan.The bulb is often linked to the Phoebus Cartel, an alliance formed in 1925 by lighting companies including Philips and General Electric. The group agreed to standardise incandescent bulbs with an expected lifespan of around 1,000 hours while also fixing prices across markets.Because the Centennial Bulb has reportedly operated for more than one million hours, conspiracy theorists argue it proves manufacturers intentionally reduced product lifespans as part of a long-running planned obsolescence strategy.However, researchers and electronics experts note that the comparison overlooks major differences in performance. The Centennial Bulb emits only a faint glow and consumes significantly less power than a standard incandescent bulb, making it unsuitable as a practical household light source.One explanation proposed by electronics and software blogger Maurycy suggests the bulb may have been manufactured with unusually high filament resistance, effectively turning it into a long-lasting night light rather than a bright everyday lamp.Lighting technology has evolved by balancing brightness, efficiency and durability rather than maximising lifespan alone. A hotter filament produces brighter, whiter light but also evaporates more quickly, reducing operating life.The later shift from incandescent bulbs to fluorescent lamps and LEDs further changed the equation. These newer technologies consume less electricity while generally lasting much longer than traditional incandescent bulbs.Although the Phoebus Cartel established a 1,000-hour standard for incandescent bulbs before dissolving around the start of World War II, experts say the Centennial Bulb's continued operation is primarily due to its unusually dim output and operating conditions, rather than evidence of a hidden manufacturing

Conspiracy theorists claim it proves manufacturers intentionally reduced product lifespans as part of a long-running planned obsolescence strategy. Experts say its low power consumption, dim output and unique construction explain why it has continued operating so long.

Article Title: China's pharma companies are facing a 'monkey problem' that they say is as tough as 'negotiating for an Nvidia chip'
Article Text:
Lab monkeys now cost $26,294 each in China, and biotech firms say sourcing them is as hard as securing Nvidia chips.

Why lab monkey prices in China have doubled inside a year

How the monkey shortage is delaying drug trials and preclinical studies

China's lab monkey shortage runs to 2028, with Cambodia imports as the fix

In June, a Chinese state laboratory paid 178,000 yuan—about $26,294—for each of 40 cynomolgus macaques. Twelve months earlier, the same animal would have cost roughly half that. Similar spikes have rippled through the industry, according to biotech executives, and the timing could hardly be worse for a country that has spent the past five years rebuilding itself into the world's fastest drug development machine.The bottleneck is not a collapse in supply. Regulated breeding farms are holding steady. What has changed is demand, and the scale of it. China now accounts for roughly a third of the global innovative drug pipeline and is the top destination for clinical trials, and every one of those programmes needs primate safety data before it goes anywhere near a human arm. Jielun Zhu, co-founder and CFO at cancer therapy developer Excalipoint Therapeutics, compared the scramble to a large language model company chasing compute. "It's like negotiating with Nvidia to secure its chips," he said.Monkeys are the gatekeepers to the clinic, and there is no workaround. Their physiological closeness to humans makes them the most reliable surrogate for toxicology work—tracking how a drug moves through the body, what it does to organs, and whether anything about it is fatal.That matters most for biologics and newer formats such as antibody-drug conjugates, bispecifics and in vivo CAR-T, the exact areas where Chinese firms have been signing blockbuster licensing deals with Western pharma. UBS Securities' China healthcare research head Chen Chen points to those categories specifically. A single programme can consume anywhere from a dozen animals to a hundred.The practical cost is time. Harri Jarvelainen, a China-based consultant who advises Western clients on preclinical work, says study planning now takes an extra four months, and in bad cases as long as ten. Part of that is regulatory: Chinese rules require monkeys used in toxicology testing to be at least three years old, so a shortfall today cannot be bred away for another three years. Speed to clinic has been the single biggest competitive advantage Chinese biotechs hold over their American rivals, and this is the one input they cannot manufacture faster.Big contract research organisations saw this coming. WuXi AppTec, Pharmaron and Joinn Laboratories all run their own breeding operations, and Joinn in July forecast a thirteen-fold jump in first-half net profit largely because the monkeys on its books are suddenly worth so much more. Zheshang Securities estimated in February that China will run short by 15,000 to 20,000 animals annually between 2026 and 2028, with imports from Cambodia—restarted this year after a pandemic-era freeze—eventually filling part of the hole.There is precedent for the cycle. During Covid, prices went from about $1,800 a monkey in 2018 to $7,000 by 2020 as vaccine programmes piled in. This time the demand is structural, not a one-off emergency, and Zhu expects a single animal to cross 200,000 yuan next year.
Article Summary: Lab monkeys now cost $26,294 each in china, and biotech firms say sourcing them is as hard as securing nvidia chips. China now accounts for roughly a third of the global innovative drug pipeline and is the top destination for clinical trials. China's lab monkey shortage runs to 2028, with cambodia imports as the fix.

Article Title: Apple releases macOS Tahoe 26.6.1 to fix Screen Sharing security flaw
Article Text:
Mac users can check for the latest update in the Settings app

How to download macOS Tahoe 26.6.1

Apple's most popular Mac is now its hardest to buy

Apple has released macOS Tahoe 26.6.1, a new security update for Mac users that fixes a vulnerability related to the Screen Sharing feature. According to Apple’s security support document, the flaw could allow an attacker to authenticate to Screen Sharing without having valid credentials. Apple says it has addressed the security issue by improving state management. The company has also released updates for older macOS versions, including macOS Sonoma 14.8.9 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.9, with the same security fix.The fix is not limited to Macs running macOS Tahoe. Apple has also released macOS Sonoma 14.8.9 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.9, which address the same Screen Sharing vulnerability. This means Mac users who have not upgraded to macOS Tahoe can also install the security fix while remaining on their existing supported macOS version.Mac users can check for the latest update by opening the System Settings app and navigating to the Software Update section. If macOS Tahoe 26.6.1 is available for the device, users can download and install it from there.Given that the update addresses a security vulnerability that could allow authentication without valid credentials, users may want to install the latest available update on their Macs.In another news, shipping estimates of Apple MacBook Air have slipped by weeks across nearly every configuration, likely because of the global memory shortage. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported in his Power On newsletter that retail sources describe Air inventory as more constrained than they can ever recall. Order a base model from Apple's online store today and delivery lands at the end of August. Buyers of the Apple MacBook Air are reportedly being told to wait till early September to get hold of the device.

Article Title: Meta AI head Alexandr Wang to American startups: Working for US government is not a matter of convenience, but basic principle
Article Text:
Meta AI head

Alexandr Wang’s Chinese companies sourcing training data from Silicon Valley firms

AI Czar David Sacks says China's Kimi K3 model is ‘concerning’ for America

Meta AI head Alexandr Wang has called on American startups to treat serving the US government as a fundamental principle rather than a commercial convenience. Reacting to a post shared by Aakash Sabharwal, VP of engineering at Scale AI, Wang said: “Serving the US government should not be a commercial convenience, it must be a bedrock principle for startups. ” Sabharwal, responding to a Forbes report on Chinese companies sourcing training data from Silicon Valley firms, warned that data companies working with the U.S. government should not also serve Chinese AI labs. “American companies should not be selling data to Chinese AI labs. @scale_AI doesn’t do this work, and we have turned down revenue because of it. The companies that do are undermining American AI leadership and risking national security,” he wrote.Alexandr Wang raised concerns after the report by Forbes revealed that Chinese companies are sourcing data from Silicon Valley firms. According to the report, sales teams from Silicon Valley's data-labeling startups encountered eager buyers from China's AI industry at this year's International Conference on Machine Learning in Seoul, with Tencent among the firms circulating detailed requests for training data covering finance, cybersecurity and self-improving AI systems.The investigation found that the same American vendors serving OpenAI, Anthropic, and in some cases the U.S. government, including firms such as Surge AI, Mercor, AfterQuery and Turing, have also supplied Chinese buyers such as Tencent, Ant Group, Alibaba and ByteDance. Citing data-labeling entrepreneurs with visibility into the market, Forbes estimated that the top six Chinese AI labs collectively spend around $500 million a year with American data-labeling companies. The report noted that while the U.S. has restricted China's access to advanced AI chips, it has not placed similar restrictions on the training data and human expertise that shape how AI models learn to perform complex tasks.Meanwhile, in related news, AI Czar David Sacks shared his views on China’s new Kimi K3 artificial intelligence (AI) model, calling its performance “concerning” for American technological dominance. Sacks warned that heavy domestic regulation is crippling US innovation just as overseas rivals catch up, drawing an immediate agreement from billionaire Elon Musk. Sacks comments came soon after Beijing promoted itself as an alternative to American supremacy in AI.“This is concerning. For the first time, a Chinese model Kimi K3 has taken #1 on the Frontend Code Arena and is scoring at or near the frontier on other benchmarks,” Sacks said in a post on X (formerly Twitter). Beijing-backed startup Moonshot AI officially open-sourced a massive 2.8 trillion-parameter system that is actively dethroning top American AI models on global coding benchmarks.“Meanwhile America is tying itself in knots: politicians and bureaucrats are banning new data centers, piling on state regulations, and pushing for new federal agencies to pre-approve frontier models,” Sacks added, purportedly pointing to US government’s decision to restrict Anthropic’s Fable 5 model to non-Americans.“This is how you lose the AI race. The rest of the world won’t play by our rules if we bog ourselves down. Permissionless innovation is how America won the internet and became the technological envy of the world. We can do it again with AI -- while addressing risks in a targeted way -- or we’ll watch our lead evaporate,” he added.
Article Summary: Chinese companies are sourcing training data from silicon valley firms, according to a report by forbes. Meta ai head alexandr wang has called on american startups to treat serving the us government as a fundamental principle rather than a commercial convenience.

Article Title: Google warns Blackstone, Bridgewater, Bain Capital, KKR, TPG, Moody's targeted by hackers through phone calls; shares hacker used for attack
Article Text:
Google warns Blackstone, Bridgewater, Bain Capital, KKR, TPG, Moody's targeted by hackers

Google’s findings revealed how hackers operated

Human element exploited

Google has revealed that ransom-seeking hackers have targeted dozens of major US financial institutions and businesses in recent weeks, including Blackstone, Bridgewater Associates, Bain Capital, KKR, TPG, and Moody’s. According to a report by Reuters, the attackers used phone calls to trick employees into revealing credentials, then deployed malicious websites tailored to each firm. “Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) continues to track UNC6671 actively conducting compromises leading to data theft extortion, despite the alleged announced retirement of the BlackFile extortion brand in May 2026. Telemetry and infrastructure analysis reveal that rather than disbanding, UNC6671 has diversified its operations across multiple extortion fronts including Redact, Pink, Helix, and Falcon,” said Google in a blog post.In a blog post, Google said the hackers operate under aliases such as Redact, Pink, Falcon, and Helix, and have recently shifted focus to private equity firms, law practices, and ratings agencies. Some companies reportedly paid ransoms, though Google did not name them. Reuters analysis of 72 malicious websites linked to the campaign showed traps designed for more than 200 companies in the past five weeks.“UNC6671 continues to rely on voice phishing (vishing) to target enterprise employees, posing as IT helpdesk staff facilitating mandatory, urgent security migrations.Significantly, the threat actor often contacts employees via their personal mobile devices. These calls lure victims to spoofed login portals where Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) infrastructure intercepts credentials and multi-factor authentication (MFA) tokens. Once session persistence is established, the actors deploy automated scripts for data exfiltration from enterprise cloud environments, including Microsoft 365 and Okta,” added Google.Cyber experts noted that the attackers rely on low-tech but effective tactics. “Because the fence is now so fancy and high-tech, we just have to trick the guard into opening the door for us,” said Lee Clark of the Retail and Hospitality ISAC. Google’s Austin Larsen added: “Really, it’s a money thing. They think these firms have sensitive data worth paying to protect.”Beyond Wall Street, firms such as Uber, Zillow, Levi Strauss, and law firms including Paul Hastings and Greenberg Traurig were also targeted. Hedge funds like Point72, Two Sigma, and Citadel were among those approached by hackers.
Article Summary: Google warns blackstone, bridgewater, bain capital, kkr, tpg, moody's targeted by hackers. Hackers operate under aliases such as redact, pink, falcon, and helix. Some companies reportedly paid ransoms, though google did not name them.

Article Title: Xiaomi announces its home and lifestyle sub-brand Mijia in India
Article Text:
Xiaomi announces its home and lifestyle sub-brand Mijia in India

Xiaomi India has announced Mijia by Xiaomi, its dedicated home and lifestyle sub-brand, in India. The announcement, the company said, strengthens its home ecosystem and marks the next phase of Xiaomi 's journey in the country. Mijia, meaning "Mi Home," is Xiaomi Group's home and lifestyle sub-brand, bringing the company's globally established smart living experience to one of its most strategic markets. In a press release, Xiaomi stated that Mijia will Xiaomi' (flagship), 'REDMI' and 'POCO' under the Xiaomi brand portfolio. Henceforth, the company’s Home and lifestyle products will carry the Mijia by Xiaomi branding, while continuing to embody the Xiaomi Group's innovation and quality standards.Xiaomi’s existing home categories, including air purifiers along with the large appliances category will be moved under the Mijia by Xiaomi sub-brand. The expanded portfolio will deliver a more connected experience, enabling seamless integration across devices while bringing better experiences to Indian consumers.Sudhin Mathur, Chief Operating Officer, Xiaomi India, said, "Over the past 12 years, Xiaomi has continuously evolved alongside Indian consumers, expanding from smartphones into a broader consumer technology portfolio. The introduction of Mijia by Xiaomi marks an important milestone in strengthening the Home dimension of our global Human × Car × Home strategy in India and reflects our long-term commitment to the market.As we deepen our presence in the category, our focus is on making connected ecosystem more intelligent, intuitive and seamless, bringing Xiaomi's global smart living experience to more homes across India."Xiaomi entered the Indian market in 2014. “The milestone reflects more than business growth; it represents Xiaomi's continued evolution alongside Indian consumers,” the company stated adding “Building on the trust of millions of consumers, the company has steadily expanded its portfolio across Smart TVs, tablets, and AIoT products, building connected experiences that reach millions of homes across the country”.Xiaomi introduced its Human × Car × Home smart ecosystem globally in 2023, a strategy that seamlessly connects personal devices, electric vehicles and smart home products through Xiaomi HyperOS. In India, the company has steadily built the 'Human' portfolio over the years through smartphones, tablets, Smart TVs and more. The company now aims to focus on strengthening the 'Home' portfolio in our Human × Car × Home ecosystem. ₠
